questions.q:
The sum of the real roots of the equation
$\left|\begin{cases}x & - 6 & - 1 \\ 2 & - 3x & x - 3 \\ - 3 & 2x & x + 2\end{cases}\right| = 0,$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given $\left|\begin{cases}x & - 6 & - 1 \\ 2 & - 3x & x - 3 \\ - 3 & 2x & x + 2\end{cases}\right| = 0$

On expansion, we get $x\left\{- 3x\left(x + 2\right) - 2x\left(x - 3\right)\right\} + 6\left\{2\left(x + 2\right) + 3\left(x - 3\right)\right\} - 1\left(4x - 9x\right) = 0$

$⇒ x\left\{- 3{x}^{2} - 6x - 2{x}^{2} + 6x\right\} + 6\left\{2x + 4 + 3x - 9\right\} - 1\left(- 5x\right) = 0$

$⇒ - 5{x}^{3} + 30x - 30 + 5x = 0$

$⇒ 5{x}^{3} - 35x + 30 = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{3} - 7x + 6 = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 1\right)\left(x - 2\right)\left(x + 3\right)$

⇒ x = 1 or $x = 2 or x = - 3 .

Here all roots \left\{1, 2, - 3\right\} are real, hence the sum of the real roots is$1 + 2 - 3 = 0 .

questions.q:
Let $\lambda$ be a real number for which the system of linear equations

$x + y + z = 6,$

$4x + \lambday - \lambdaz = \lambda - 2$ and

$3x + 2y - 4z = - 5$

has infinitely many solutions. Then $\lambda$ is a root of the quadratic equation:
questions.solution:
The system of equations ${a}_{1}x + {b}_{1}y + {c}_{1}z + {d}_{1} = 0, {a}_{2}x + {b}_{2}y + {c}_{2}z + {d}_{2} = 0$ and ${a}_{3}x + {b}_{3}y + {c}_{3}z + {d}_{3} = 0$ have a infinitely many solution, if

$D = \left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right| = 0, {D}_{1} = \left|\begin{cases}{d}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {d}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {d}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right| = 0, {D}_{2} = \left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {d}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {d}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {d}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right| = 0$ and ${D}_{3} = \left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {d}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {d}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {d}_{3}\end{cases}\right| = 0 .$

Thus, for infinitely many solutions, we have $D = 0$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & \lambda & - \lambda \\ 3 & 2 & - 4\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 1\left(- 4\lambda + 2\lambda\right) - 1\left(- 16 + 3\lambda\right) + 1\left(8 - 3\lambda\right) = 0$

$⇒ - 2\lambda + 16 - 3\lambda + 8 - 3\lambda = 0$

$⇒ 24 - 3\lambda = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 3$

And, $\lambda = 3$ satisfies the equation ${\lambda}^{2} - \lambda - 6 = 0 .$

questions.solution:
$∆ = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & \lambda\end{cases}\right| = \left(\lambda - 3\right)$
${∆}_{1} = \left|\begin{cases}5 & 1 & 1 \\ 6 & 2 & 2 \\ \mu & 3 & \lambda\end{cases}\right| = 4\left(\lambda - 3\right)$
${∆}_{3} = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 5 & 1 \\ 1 & 6 & 2 \\ 1 & \mu & \lambda\end{cases}\right| = \lambda - \mu + 4$
${∆}_{4} = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & 6 \\ 1 & 3 & \mu\end{cases}\right| = \mu - 7$
For infinite many solution $∆ = {∆}_{1} = {∆}_{2} = {∆}_{3} = 0$
$⇒ \lambda = 3, \text{ and } \mu = 7$ from $∆ = 0 \text{ and } {∆}_{4} = 0$
& $\lambda = 3, \mu = 7$ Satisfies ${∆}_{3} = 0 = {∆}_{1}$
$∴ \lambda + \mu = 10$

questions.solution:
${\Delta}_{1} = \left|\begin{cases}x & sin\theta \\ - sin\theta & - x \\ cos\theta & 1\end{cases}\begin{array}{ll}cos\theta \\ 1 \\ x\end{array}\right|$
$= x\left(- {x}^{2} - 1\right) - sin\theta\left(- xsin\theta - cos\theta\right) + cos\theta ( - sin\theta + xcos\theta )$
$= - {x}^{3} - x + xsi{n}^{2}\theta + sin\thetacos ⁡ \theta - sin\thetacos\theta + xco{s}^{2}\theta$
$= - {x}^{3} - x + x\left(\sin^{2} ⁡ \theta + \cos^{2} ⁡ \theta\right)$
$= - {x}^{3}$
Similarly: ${\Delta}_{2} = - {x}^{3}$
$∴ {\Delta}_{1} + {\Delta}_{2} = - 2{x}^{3}$

questions.q: If the system of equations $2x + 3y - z = 0, x + ky - 2z = 0 and 2x - y + z = 0$ has a non-trivial solution $\left(x, y, z\right),$ then $\dfrac{x}{y} + \dfrac{y}{z} + \dfrac{z}{x} + k$ is equal to
questions.solution:
The system of equations ${a}_{1}x + {b}_{1}y + {c}_{1}z = 0, {a}_{2}x + {b}_{2}y + {c}_{2}z = 0$ and ${a}_{3}x + {b}_{3}y + {c}_{3}z = 0$ has a non-trivial solution, if

$\left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right| = 0 .$

Hence, for the given lines $2x + 3y - z = 0, x + ky - 2z = 0$ and $2x - y + z = 0,$ we have

$\left|\begin{cases}2 & 3 & - 1 \\ 1 & k & - 2 \\ 2 & - 1 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 2\left(k - 2\right) - 3\left(1 + 4\right) - 1\left(- 1 - 2k\right) = 0$

$⇒ 2k - 4 - 15 + 1 + 2k = 0$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{9}{2}$

Thus, the lines are

$2x + 3y - z = 0 . . . \left(1\right)$

$x + \dfrac{9}{2}y - 2z = 0 . . . \left(2\right)$

$2x - y + z = 0 . . . \left(3\right)$

$\left(1\right) - \left(3\right) ⇒ 4y - 2z = 0$

$2y = z . . . \left(4\right)$

$\dfrac{y}{z} = \dfrac{1}{2} . . . \left(5\right)$

put $z$ from eq $\left(4\right)$ into $\left(1\right)$

$2x + 3y - 2y = 0$

$2x + y = 0$

$\dfrac{x}{y} = - \dfrac{1}{2} . . . \left(6\right)$

From eq $\left(4\right)$ and $\left(6\right)$

$\dfrac{z}{x} = - 4$

Hence, $\dfrac{x}{y} + \dfrac{y}{z} + \dfrac{z}{x} + k = - \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} - 4 + \dfrac{9}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} .$

Hence, for the given lines $2x + 3y - z = 0, x + ky - 2z = 0$ and $2x - y + z = 0,$ we have

$\left|\begin{cases}2 & 3 & - 1 \\ 1 & k & - 2 \\ 2 & - 1 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 2\left(k - 2\right) - 3\left(1 + 4\right) - 1\left(- 1 - 2k\right) = 0$

$⇒ 2k - 4 - 15 + 1 + 2k = 0$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{9}{2}$

Thus, the lines are

$2x + 3y - z = 0 . . . \left(1\right)$

$x + \dfrac{9}{2}y - 2z = 0 . . . \left(2\right)$

$2x - y + z = 0 . . . \left(3\right)$

$\left(1\right) - \left(3\right) ⇒ 4y - 2z = 0$

$2y = z . . . \left(4\right)$

$\dfrac{y}{z} = \dfrac{1}{2} . . . \left(5\right)$

put $z$ from eq $\left(4\right)$ into $\left(1\right)$

$2x + 3y - 2y = 0$

$2x + y = 0$

$\dfrac{x}{y} = - \dfrac{1}{2} . . . \left(6\right)$

From eq $\left(4\right)$ and $\left(6\right)$

$\dfrac{z}{x} = - 4$

Hence, $\dfrac{x}{y} + \dfrac{y}{z} + \dfrac{z}{x} + k = - \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} - 4 + \dfrac{9}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} .$

questions.q: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of the equation ${x}^{2} + x + 1 = 0 .$ Then for $y \ne 0$ in $R, \left|\begin{cases}y + 1 & \alpha & \beta \\ \alpha & y + \beta & 1 \\ \beta & 1 & y + \alpha\end{cases}\right|$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Roots of the equation ${x}^{2} + x + 1 = 0$ are $\alpha$ and $\beta$ and we know that the sum of roots of a quadratic equation $a{x}^{2} + bx + c = 0$ is $- \dfrac{b}{a}$ and $\dfrac{c}{a}$ respectively.

$⇒ \alpha + \beta = - 1$ and $\alpha\beta = 1 .$

Now, let $∆ = \left|\begin{cases}y + 1 & \alpha & \beta \\ \alpha & y + \beta & 1 \\ \beta & 1 & y + \alpha\end{cases}\right|$

Applying ${R}_{1} \to {R}_{1} + {R}_{2} + {R}_{3},$ we get

$∆ = \left|\begin{cases}y + 1 + \alpha + \beta & y + 1 + \alpha + \beta & y + 1 + \alpha + \beta \\ \alpha & y + \beta & 1 \\ \beta & 1 & y + \alpha\end{cases}\right|$

$= \left(y + 1 + \alpha + \beta\right)\left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ \alpha & y + \beta & 1 \\ \beta & 1 & y + \alpha\end{cases}\right|$

$= \left(y + 1 + \left(- 1\right)\right)\left[1\left\{\left(y + \beta\right)\left(y + \alpha\right) - 1\right\} - 1\left\{\alpha\left(y + \alpha\right) - \beta\right\} + 1\left\{\alpha - \beta\left(y + \beta\right)\right\}\right]$

$= y\left[{y}^{2} + \left(\alpha + \beta\right)y + \alpha\beta - y\alpha - {\alpha}^{2} + \beta + \alpha - \betay - {\beta}^{2}\right]$

$= y\left[{y}^{2} + \left(\alpha + \beta\right)y + \alpha\beta - y\left(\alpha + \beta + 1\right) - \left({\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2}\right) + \left(\alpha + \beta\right)\right]$

On putting the values of $\alpha + \beta \text{ and } \alpha\beta,$ we get

$= y\left[{y}^{2} + \left(- 1\right)y + 1 - y\left(- 1 + 1\right) - \left({\left(\alpha + \beta\right)}^{2} - 2\alpha\beta\right) + \left(- 1\right)\right]$

$= y\left[{y}^{2} - y + 1 - \left({\left(- 1\right)}^{2} - 2\right) - 1\right]$

$= y\left[{y}^{2} - y + 1\right]$

$= {y}^{3}$ (on simplifying)

Applying ${R}_{1} \to {R}_{1} + {R}_{2} + {R}_{3},$ we get

$∆ = \left|\begin{cases}y + 1 + \alpha + \beta & y + 1 + \alpha + \beta & y + 1 + \alpha + \beta \\ \alpha & y + \beta & 1 \\ \beta & 1 & y + \alpha\end{cases}\right|$

$= \left(y + 1 + \alpha + \beta\right)\left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ \alpha & y + \beta & 1 \\ \beta & 1 & y + \alpha\end{cases}\right|$

$= \left(y + 1 + \left(- 1\right)\right)\left[1\left\{\left(y + \beta\right)\left(y + \alpha\right) - 1\right\} - 1\left\{\alpha\left(y + \alpha\right) - \beta\right\} + 1\left\{\alpha - \beta\left(y + \beta\right)\right\}\right]$

$= y\left[{y}^{2} + \left(\alpha + \beta\right)y + \alpha\beta - y\alpha - {\alpha}^{2} + \beta + \alpha - \betay - {\beta}^{2}\right]$

On putting the values of $\alpha + \beta \text{ and } \alpha\beta,$ we get

$= y\left[{y}^{2} + \left(- 1\right)y + 1 - y\left(- 1 + 1\right) - \left({\left(\alpha + \beta\right)}^{2} - 2\alpha\beta\right) + \left(- 1\right)\right]$

$= y\left[{y}^{2} - y + 1 - \left({\left(- 1\right)}^{2} - 2\right) - 1\right]$

$= y\left[{y}^{2} - y + 1\right]$

$= {y}^{3}$ (on simplifying)

questions.q: Let the numbers $2, b, c$ be in an A.P. and $A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & b & c \\ 4 & {b}^{2} & {c}^{2}\end{cases}\right]$ . If $det ( A ) \in [ 2,16 ] ,$ then $c$ lies in the interval:
questions.solution:
$\left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & b & c \\ 4 & {b}^{2} & {c}^{2}\end{cases}\right|\overset{{C}_{2} \to {C}_{2} - {C}_{1}, {C}_{3} \to {C}_{3} - {C}_{1}}{\to}\left|\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & b - 2 & c - 2 \\ 4 & {b}^{2} - 4 & {c}^{2} - 4\end{cases}\right| = \left(b - 2\right)\left(c - 2\right)\left(c - b\right)$
Let common difference of $AP = d$
$∴ b = 2 + d, c = 2 + 2d$
$\left|A\right| = d \times 2d \times d = 2{d}^{3} \in \left[2, 16\right]$
$⇒ {d}^{3} \in \left[1, 8\right] ⇒ d \in \left[1, 2\right] ⇒ 2d \in \left[2, 4\right]$
$⇒ 2 + 2d \in \left[4, 6\right]$
$∴ c \in \left[4, 6\right]$

questions.q:
If the system of linear equations
$x - 2y + kz = 1$
$2x + y + z = 2$
$3x - y - kz = 3$
has a solution $\left(x, y, z\right), z \ne 0,$ then $\left(x, y\right)$ lies on the straight line whose equation is:
questions.solution:
$x - 2y + kz = 1$ .........(1)
$2x + y + z = 2$ .........(2)
$3x - y - kz = 3$ ........(3)

Hence,

$\left[\begin{cases}1 & - 2 & k \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & - 1 & - k\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}x \\ y \\ z\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{array}\right]$

For infinite solution,

$\left|\begin{cases}1 & - 2 & k \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & - 1 & - k\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left(- k + 1\right) + 2\left(- 2k - 3\right) + k\left(- 2 - 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ k = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

Put this value in the equation $\left(1\right)$, we get

$2x - 4y - z = 2 . . . . \left(4\right)$

Adding the equation $\left(4\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$, we get

$4x - 3y = 4$

Hence, the equation of straight line is $4x - 3y - 4 = 0$

questions.q: The greatest value of $c \in R$ for which the system of linear equations $x - cy - cz = 0$, $cx - y + cz = 0$, $cx + cy - z = 0$ has a non-trivial solution, is
questions.solution:
$∵$ System of equation has non trivial solution. It is possible only when $∆ = 0$.
$∴ ∆ = \left|\begin{cases}1 & - c & - c \\ c & - 1 & c \\ c & c & - 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$
$⇒ 1\left(1 - {c}^{2}\right) + c\left(- c - {c}^{2}\right) - c\left({c}^{2} + c\right) = 0$
$⇒ {2c}^{3} + 3{c}^{2} - 1 = 0$
$⇒ c = - 1, \dfrac{1}{2}$

Hence, the greatest value of $c = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

$A=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}1 & \sin \theta & 1 \\ -\sin \theta & 1 & \sin \theta \\ -1 & -\sin \theta & 1\end{array}\right]$
$\Rightarrow \operatorname{det}(A)=\left(11+\sin ^2 \theta\right)-\sin \theta(-\sin \theta+\sin \theta)+1\left(\sin ^2 \theta+1\right)$
$=2+2 \sin ^2 \theta$
$\because \theta \in\left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}, \frac{5 \pi}{4}\right)$
$\therefore \sin 2 \theta \in\left[0, \frac{1}{2}\right]$
$\therefore \operatorname{det}(A) \in[2,3]$ which is a subset of $\left(\frac{3}{2}, 3\right]$

The set of all values of $\lambda$ for which the system of linear equations
$x - 2y - 2z = \lambdax$
$x + 2y + z = \lambday$
$- x - y = \lambdaz$
has a non-trivial solution :
questions.solution:
For non-trivial solution, $∆ = 0$.

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}1 - \lambda & - 2 & - 2 \\ 1 & 2 - \lambda & 1 \\ - 1 & - 1 & - \lambda\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left(1 - \lambda\right)\left(- 2\lambda + {\lambda}^{2} + 1\right) + 1\left(- \lambda + 1\right) - 1\left(- 1 + 2 - \lambda\right) = 0$

$⇒ {\lambda}^{2} - 3{\lambda}^{2} + 3\lambda - 1 = 0$

$⇒ {\left(\lambda - 1\right)}^{3} = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 1$

Singleton set

Let $A and B$ be two invertible matrices of order $3 \times 3$. If $\operatorname{det}\left(\mathrm{ABA}^{\mathrm{T}}\right)=8$ and det $\left(\mathrm{AB}^{-1}\right)=8$, then det $\left(\mathrm{BA}^{-1} \mathrm{~B}^{\mathrm{T}}\right)$ is

equal to
questions.solution:
Let $|A|=a,|B|=b \left.\Rightarrow \quad \mid A^{\eta}\right\rceil=a\left|A^{-1}\right|=\frac{1}{a},\left|B^{\eta}\right|=b,\left|B^{-1}\right|=\frac{1}{b} \because \quad A B A^{\eta}=8 \Rightarrow|A||B| \mid A^{\eta}-8 \ldots(1) \Rightarrow \quad a \cdot b \cdot a=8 \Rightarrow a^{2} b=8 \because \quad A B^{-1}|=8 \Rightarrow H|\left|B^{-1}\right|=8 \Rightarrow a, \frac{1}{b}=8$

From (1) \& (2)

$a=4, b=\frac{1}{2}$

Then, $\left|B A^{-1} B^{\eta}\right|=|B|\left|A^{-1}\right|\left|B^{\eta}\right|=b \cdot \frac{1}{a} \cdot b=\frac{b^{2}}{a}=\frac{1}{16}$

questions.q: Let $A = \left[\begin{cases}2 & b & 1 \\ b & {b}^{2} + 1 & b \\ 1 & b & 2\end{cases}\right],$ where $b > 0$. Then the minimum value of $\dfrac{det\left(A\right)}{b}$ is:
questions.solution:
$\left|A\right| = \left|\begin{cases}2 & b & 1 \\ b & {b}^{2} + 1 & b \\ 1 & b & 2\end{cases}\right|$

$= 2\left(2{b}^{2} + 2 - {b}^{2}\right) - b\left(2b - b\right) + 1\left({b}^{2} - {b}^{2} - 1\right)$

$= 2\left({b}^{2} + 2\right) - {b}^{2} - 1$

$= 2{b}^{2} + 4 - {b}^{2} - 1$

$= {b}^{2} + 3$

$\dfrac{\left|A\right|}{b} = b + \dfrac{3}{b} = {\left(\sqrt{b} - \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{b}}\right)}^{2} + 2\sqrt{3}$

Hence, the minimum value of $\dfrac{\left|A\right|}{b}$ is $2\sqrt{3}$. $\left(∵ {\left(\sqrt{b} - \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{b}}\right)}^{2} \ge 0\right)$

questions.q: If the system of equations $x + y + z = 5,$x + 2y + 3z = 9,$x + 3y + \alphaz = \beta$ has inifinitely many solutions, then $\beta - \alpha$ equals
questions.solution:
The system of linear equations ${a}_{1}x + {b}_{1}y + {c}_{1}z + {d}_{1} = 0, {a}_{2}x + {b}_{2}y + {c}_{2}z + {d}_{2} = 0$ and ${a}_{3}x + {b}_{3}y + {c}_{3}z + {d}_{3} = 0$ have infinitely many solutions, if

$D = \left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right| = 0, {D}_{1} = \left|\begin{cases}{d}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {d}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {d}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right| = 0, {D}_{2} = \left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {d}_{1} & {c}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {d}_{2} & {c}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {d}_{3} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}\right| = 0$

and ${D}_{3} = \left|\begin{cases}{a}_{1} & {b}_{1} & {d}_{1} \\ {a}_{2} & {b}_{2} & {d}_{2} \\ {a}_{3} & {b}_{3} & {d}_{3}\end{cases}\right| = 0 .$

Hence, for the system of equations $x + y + z = 5, x + 2y + 3z = 9$ and $x + 3y + \alphaz = \beta$ have infinitely many solution, if

$D = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & \alpha\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left(2\alpha - 9\right) - \left(\alpha - 3\right) + \left(3 - 2\right)$

$⇒ 2\alpha - 9 - \alpha + 3 + 1 = 0$

$⇒ \alpha = 5 .$

And, ${D}_{1} = \left|\begin{cases}5 & 1 & 1 \\ 9 & 2 & 3 \\ \beta & 3 & \alpha\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}5 & 1 & 1 \\ 9 & 2 & 3 \\ \beta & 3 & 5\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ 5\left(10 - 9\right) - \left(45 - 3\beta\right) + \left(27 - 2\beta\right) = 0$

$⇒ 5 - 45 + 3\beta + 27 - 2\beta = 0$

$⇒ \beta = 13 .$

Hence, $\beta - \alpha = 13 - 5 = 8 .$

questions.q: Let $d \in R,$ and $A = \left[\begin{cases}- 2 & 4 + d & \left(sin\theta\right) - 2 \\ 1 & \left(sin\theta\right) + 2 & d \\ 5 & \left(2sin\theta\right) - d & \left(- sin\theta\right) + 2 + 2d\end{cases}\right],$\theta \in \left[0, 2\pi\right] .$ If the minimum value of $det\left(A\right)$ is $8,$ then a value of $d$ is:
questions.solution:
$\left|A\right| = \left|\begin{cases}- 2 & 4 + d & \left(sin\theta\right) - 2 \\ 1 & \left(sin\theta\right) + 2 & d \\ 5 & \left(2sin\theta\right) - d & \left(- sin\theta\right) + 2 + 2d\end{cases}\right|$

${R}_{3} \to {R}_{3} - 2{R}_{2} + {R}_{1}$

$= \left|\begin{cases}- 2 & 4 + d & \left(sin\theta\right) - 2 \\ 1 & \left(sin\theta\right) + 2 & d \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{cases}\right|$

$= 1\left\{\left(4 + d\right)d - \left(sin\theta + 2\right)\left(sin\theta - 2\right)\right\}$

$= 4d + {d}^{2} - \sin^{2}\theta + 4 = {\left(d + 2\right)}^{2} - \sin^{2}\theta$

We know that $0 \le \sin^{2}\theta \le 1$

Given, the minimum value of $\left|A\right| = 8,$ which is possible, when $\sin^{2}\theta = 1$

$⇒ {\left(d + 2\right)}^{2} = 9$

$⇒ d + 2 = \pm 3$

$⇒ d = 1$ or $d = - 5 .$

questions.q: If the system of linear equations $x - 4y + 7z = g$; $3y - 5z = h$; $- 2x + 5y - 9z = k$ is consistent, then:
questions.solution:
$x - 4y + 7z = g$ ...(i)

$3y - 5z = h$ ...(ii)

$- 2x + 5y - 9z = k$ ...(iii)

(i) + (ii), we get

$x - y + 2z = g + h$ ...(iv)

(ii) - (iii), we get

$2x - 2y + 4z = h - k$

$⇒ x - y + 2z = \dfrac{h - k}{2}$ ...(v)

Since, coefficient of $x, y, z$ in (iv) and (v) are same. Hence, for system to be consistent

$g + h = \dfrac{h - k}{2}$

$⇒ 2g + 2h = h - k$

$⇒ 2g + h + k = 0$

questions.solution:
For no solution

$\dfrac{k + 2}{k} = \dfrac{10}{k + 3} = \dfrac{k}{k - 1}$

$⇒ \left(k + 2\right)\left(k + 3\right) = 10k$

$⇒ {k}^{2} - 5k + 6 = 0 ⇒ k = 2, 3$

$k \ne 2$ for $k = 2$ both lines are identical.

So, only $k = 3$ is possible.

So the number of values of $k$ is $1$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\cos x & x & 1 \\ 2 \sin x & x^2 & 2 x \\ \tan x & x & 1\end{array}\right|$, then $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{x}$
options:
Exists and is equal to $-2$

Does not exist

Exist and is equal to 0

 Exists and is equal to 2
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & f(x)=\left|$\begin{array}{ccc}$\cos x$ & x & 1 \\ 2 $\sin x$ & x^2 & 2 x \\ $\tan x$ & x & 1\end{array}$\right| \\=& \cos x\left(x^2-2 x^2\right)-x(2 \sin x-2 x \tan x) \\=&-x^2 \cos x-2 x \sin x+2 x^2 \tan x \\\left.+2 x \sin x-x^2 \tan x\right) \\=& x^2 \tan x-x^2 \tan x \\ \Rightarrow & f^{\prime}(x)=2 x(\tan x-\cos x)+x^2\left(\sec ^2 x+\sin x\right) \\ \therefore & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{x} \\=& \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{2 x(\tan x-\cos x)+x^2\left(\sec ^2 x+\sin x\right)}{x} \\=& \lim _{x \rightarrow 0}(\tan x-\cos x)+x\left(\sec ^2 x+\sin x\right) \\=& 2(0-1)+0=-2 \\ \text{ So, } \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{f^{\prime}(x)}{x}=-2 \end{aligned}$

questions.q:
If the system of linear equations

$x + ky + 3z = 0$
$3x + ky - 2z = 0$
$2x + 4y - 3z = 0$

has a non-zero solution $\left(x, y, z\right),$ then $\dfrac{xz}{{y}^{2}}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
$\left|\begin{cases}1 & k & 3 \\ 3 & k & - 2 \\ 2 & 4 & - 3\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left(- 3k + 8\right) - 3\left(- 3k - 12\right) + 2\left(- 5k\right) = 0$

$⇒ - 4k + 44 = 0$⇒$k = 11$

$⇒ x + 11y + 3z = 0 . . . \left(1\right)$

$⇒ 3x + 11y - 2z = 0 . . . \left(2\right)$

$⇒ 2x + 4y - 3z = 0 . . . \left(3\right)$

On solving equations$\left(1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$, we get

$2x - 5z = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{5z}{2}$

Put it in equation $\left(3\right)$, we get

$2z + 4y = 0$

$⇒ z = - 2y$

$∴ \dfrac{xz}{{y}^{2}} = \dfrac{\left(- 2y\right) \times \left(- 5y\right)}{{y}^{2}} = 10$

$\left|\begin{cases}x - 4 & 2x & 2x \\ 2x & x - 4 & 2x \\ 2x & 2x & x - 4\end{cases}\right| = \left(A + Bx\right){\left(x - A\right)}^{2}$

Put $x = 0 ⇒ \left|\begin{cases}- 4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & - 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & - 4\end{cases}\right| = {A}^{3} ⇒ A = - 4$

$\left|\begin{cases}x - 4 & 2x & 2x \\ 2x & x - 4 & 2x \\ 2x & 2x & x - 4\end{cases}\right| = \left(Bx - 4\right){\left(x + 4\right)}^{2}$

$\left|\begin{cases}1 - \dfrac{4}{x} & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 - \dfrac{4}{x} & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 - \dfrac{4}{x}\end{cases}\right| = \left(B - \dfrac{4}{x}\right){\left(1 + \dfrac{4}{x}\right)}^{2}$

Put $x \to \infty ⇒ \left|\begin{cases}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 1\end{cases}\right| = B$

$x + y + z = 0$
Such that the point $\left(a, b, c\right)$ lies on the plane $x + 2y + z = 6$ , then $2a + b + c$ equals:
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{ll}x + 8y + 7z = 0 . . . \left(i\right) \\ 9x + 2y + 3z = 0 . . . \left(ii\right) \\ x + y + z = 0 . . . \left(iii\right)\end{array}$.....

Solve the equation $\left(i\right) \text{ and } \left(iii\right)$

$⇒ 7y + 6z = 0$

Solve the equation $\left(ii\right) \text{ and } \left(iii\right)$

$⇒ 7x + z = 0$

$x = \lambda \text{ and } \left|y = \dfrac{- 6\left(- 7\lambda\right)}{7}\right| \text{ and } z = - 7\lambda$

$\begin{cases}x = \lambda & \text{ and } y = 6\lambda & \text{ and } z = - 7\lambda\end{cases}$

$\begin{array}{ll}⇒ \lambda + 12\lambda - 7\lambda = 6 \\ ⇒ 6\lambda = 6 \\ ⇒ \lambda = 1\end{array} |\begin{array}{ll}⇒ 2\lambda + 6\lambda - 7\lambda \\ ⇒ \lambda = 1\end{array}$

Hence, $a = 1, b = 6, c = - 7$

$∴ 2a + b + c = 1$

questions.q: If $S = \left\{x \in \left[0, 2\pi\right]: \left|\begin{cases}0 & cos ⁡ x & - sin ⁡ x \\ sin ⁡ x & 0 & cos ⁡ x \\ cos ⁡ x & sin ⁡ x & 0\end{cases}\right| = 0\right\},$ then $\mathop{∑}_{x \in S}tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3} + x\right)$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given,$\left|\begin{cases}0 & cos ⁡ x & - sin ⁡ x \\ sin ⁡ x & 0 & cos ⁡ x \\ cos ⁡ x & sin ⁡ x & 0\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expanding the determinant,

$⇒ 0 ( 0 - cos ⁡ xsin ⁡ x ) - cos ⁡ x\left(0 - \cos^{2} ⁡ x\right) - sin ⁡ x\left(\sin^{2} ⁡ x - 0\right) = 0$

$⇒$\cos^{3} ⁡ x - \sin^{3} ⁡ x = 0$

$⇒$\tan^{3} ⁡ x = 1 ⇒ tan ⁡ x = 1 ⇒ x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}, \dfrac{5\pi}{4} ⇒ S = \left\{\dfrac{\pi}{4}, \dfrac{5\pi}{4}\right\}$

$∴ \mathop{∑}_{x \in S}tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3} + x\right)$

$= \mathop{∑}_{x \in S}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3} + tanx}{1 - \sqrt{3}tanx}\right)$

$= 2\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{1 - \sqrt{3}}\right) = - 4 - 2\sqrt{3}$

questions.q:
If $S$ is the set of distinct values of $b$ for which the following system of linear equations

$x + y + z = 1$

$x + ay + z = 1$

$ax + by + z = 0$

has no solution, then $S$ is:
options: A finite set containing two or more elements
questions.solution:
For no solution $D = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & a & 1 \\ a & b & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expanding the determinant along the first row, we get $D = - {\left(a - 1\right)}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ a = 1$

For $a = 1$, first two planes are coincident.

Now, we have $x + y + z = 1 \text{ and } ax + by + z = 0$

For no solution, these two planes are parallel.

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{a} = \dfrac{1}{b} = \dfrac{1}{1}$

$⇒ a = 1 \text{ and } b = 1$.

$∴ b = \left\{1\right\} ⇒$it is a singleton set

questions.solution:
Given equation $\left|\begin{cases}cosx & sinx & sinx \\ sinx & cosx & sinx \\ sinx & sinx & cosx\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Performing row and column operations

${R}_{1} \to {R}_{1} - {R}_{2}$

${R}_{2} \to {R}_{2} - {R}_{3}$

$⇒\left|\begin{cases}cosx - sinx & sinx - cosx & 0 \\ 0 & cosx - sinx & sinx - cosx \\ sinx & sinx & cosx\end{cases}\right| = 0$

${C}_{2} \to {C}_{2} + {C}_{3}$

$⇒\left|\begin{cases}cosx - sinx & sinx - cosx & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & sinx - cosx \\ sinx & sinx + cosx & cosx\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expanding using second row, we get

$\left(sinx + cosx\right)\left(cosx - sinx\right) - sinx\left(sinx - cosx\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(cosx - sinx\right)\left(sinx + cosx + sinx\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(cosx - sinx\right)\left(2sinx + cosx\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(cosx - sinx\right) = 0$

$sinx = cosx ⇒ \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Or

$2sinx + cosx = 0$

$tanx = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$x = \tan^{- 1}\left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

Hence, $2$ solutions are there.

questions.q: The least value of the product $xyz$ (such that $x, y\text{and}z$ are positive real numbers) for which the determinant $\left|\begin{array}{ll}x \\ 1 \\ 1\end{array}\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ y \\ 1\end{array}\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1 \\ z\end{array}$\right|$ is non-negative is$
questions.solution:
Since $A . M \ge G . M$

$\dfrac{x + y + z}{3} \ge \left(xyz\right)\dfrac{1}{3}$

$x + y + z \ge 3\left(xyz\right)\dfrac{1}{3}$

Now, $\left|\begin{array}{ll}x \\ 1 \\ 1\end{array}\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ y \\ 1\end{array}\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1 \\ z\end{array}\right| = xyz - \left(x + y + z\right) + 2$

Now determinant is non-negative

$⇒ xyz - \left(x + y + z\right) + 2 \ge 0$

$⇒ xyz - \left(3\right)\left(xyz\right)\dfrac{1}{3} + 2 \ge 0$

Let $xyz = {t}^{3}$

So, ${t}^{3} - 3t + 2 \ge 0$

$⇒ \left(t + 2\right) ( {t}^{2} - 2t + 1 ) \ge 0 ⇒ \left(t + 2\right){( t - 1 )}^{2} \ge 0$

$⇒ t \ge - 2$

$⇒ {t}^{3} \ge - 8$

$⇒$ Least value of $xyz = - 8$

questions.q:
The set of all values of $\lambda$ for which the system of linear equations:
$2 {x}_{1} - 2 {x}_{2} + {x}_{3} = \lambda {x}_{1}$
$2 {x}_{1} - 3 {x}_{2} + {2 x}_{3} = \lambda {x}_{2}$
$- {x}_{1} + {2 x}_{2} = \lambda {x}_{3}$
has a non-trivial solution,
questions.solution:
$\left(2 - \lambda\right) {x}_{1} - 2 {x}_{2} + {x}_{3} = 0$

$2 {x}_{1} - \left(\lambda + 3\right) {x}_{2} + 2 {x}_{3} = 0$

$- {x}_{1} + 2 {x}_{2} - \lambda {x}_{3} = 0$

The systems of linear equations will have a non-trivial solution

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}2 - \lambda & - 2 & 1 \\ 2 & - \lambda - 3 & 2 \\ - 1 & 2 & - \lambda\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left(2 - \lambda\right) \left[{\lambda}^{2} + 3 \lambda - 4\right] + 2 \left[- 2 \lambda + 2\right] + 1 \left[4 - \lambda - 3\right] = 0$

$2 {\lambda}^{2} + 6 \lambda - 8 - {\lambda}^{3} - 3 {\lambda}^{2} + 4 \lambda - 4 \lambda + 4 + 1 - \lambda = 0$

$- {\lambda}^{3} - {\lambda}^{2} + 5 \lambda - 3 = 0$

${\lambda}^{3} + {\lambda}^{2} - 5 \lambda + 3 = 0$

$\left(\lambda - 1\right) \left({\lambda}^{2} + 2 \lambda - 3\right) = 0$

$\left(\lambda - 1\right) \left(\lambda + 3\right) \left(\lambda - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = -3 , 1 , 1$

questions.q: If ${\Delta}_{r} = \left|\begin{cases}r & 2r - 1 & 3r - 2 \\ \dfrac{n}{2} & n - 1 & a \\ \dfrac{1}{2}n\left(n - 1\right) & {\left(n - 1\right)}^{2} & \dfrac{1}{2}\left(n - 1\right)\left(3n + 4\right)\end{cases}\right|$, then the value of $\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n - 1}{\Delta}_{r}$
questions.solution:
${\Delta}_{r} = \left|\begin{cases}r & \left(2r - 1\right) & \left(3r - 2\right) \\ \dfrac{n}{2} & \left(n - 1\right) & a \\ \dfrac{1}{2}n\left(n - 1\right) & {\left(n - 1\right)}^{2} & \dfrac{1}{2}\left(n - 1\right)\left(3n + 4\right)\end{cases}\right|$

Since, the second and the third rows are independent of $r,$ hence the sum is applied to the first row only.

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n - 1}{\Delta}_{r} = \left|\begin{cases}\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n - 1}r & 2\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n - 1}r - \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n - 1}1 & 3\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n - 1}r - 2\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n - 1}1 \\ \dfrac{n}{2} & \left(n - 1\right) & a \\ \dfrac{1}{2}n\left(n - 1\right) & {\left(n - 1\right)}^{2} & \dfrac{1}{2}\left(n - 1\right)\left(3n + 4\right)\end{cases}\right|$

Using $\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}r = \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2},$ we get

$\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n - 1}{\Delta}_{r}=\left|\begin{cases}\dfrac{\left(n - 1\right)n}{2} & \dfrac{2\left(n - 1\right)n}{2} - \left(n - 1\right) & \dfrac{3\left(n - 1\right)n}{2} - 2\left(n - 1\right) \\ \dfrac{n}{2} & \left(n - 1\right) & a \\ \dfrac{1}{2}n\left(n - 1\right) & {\left(n - 1\right)}^{2} & \dfrac{1}{2}\left(n - 1\right)\left(3n + 4\right)\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n - 1}{\Delta}_{r}=\left|\begin{cases}\dfrac{1}{2}n\left(n - 1\right) & {\left(n - 1\right)}^{2} & \dfrac{1}{2}\left(n - 1\right)\left(3n + 4\right) \\ \dfrac{n}{2} & \left(n - 1\right) & a \\ \dfrac{1}{2}n\left(n - 1\right) & {\left(n - 1\right)}^{2} & \dfrac{1}{2}\left(n - 1\right)\left(3n + 4\right)\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n - 1}{\Delta}_{r} = 0,$( ∵ {R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{3}$ are identical$)$

Hence, the sum is independent of both $n$ and $a .$

questions.q:
If $
\begin{aligned}
&\left.\mid \begin{array}{ccc}
a^2 & b^2 & c^2 \\
(a+\lambda)^2 & (b+\lambda)^2 & \left(c+\lambda^2\right) \\
(a-\lambda)^2 & \left(b-\lambda^2\right) & \left(-\lambda^2\right.
\end{array}\right) \\
&=k \lambda\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
a^2 & b^2 & c^2 \\
a & b & c \\
1 & 1 & 1
\end{array}\right|, \lambda \neq 0
\end{aligned}
$
then $\mathrm{k}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Let $\Delta=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}a^2 & b^2 & c^2 \\ (a+\lambda)^2 & (b+\lambda)^2 & (c+\lambda)^2 \\ (a-\lambda)^2 & (b-\lambda)^2 & (c-\lambda)^2\end{array}\right|$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text { Apply } \mathrm{R}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{R}_2-\mathrm{R}_3 \\
&\Delta=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
a^2 & b^2 & c^2 \\
(a+\lambda)^2-(a-\lambda)^2 & (b+\lambda)^2-(b-\lambda)^2 & (c+\lambda)^2-(c-\lambda)^2 \\
(a-\lambda)^2 & (b-\lambda)^2 & (c-\lambda)^2
\end{array}\right| \\
&=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
a^2 & b^2 & c^2 \\
4 a \lambda & 4 b \lambda & 4 c \lambda \\
(a-\lambda)^2 & (b-\lambda)^2 & (c-\lambda)^2
\end{array}\right| \\
&\left(\because(x+y)^2-(x-y)^2=4 x y\right) \\
&
\end{aligned}
$
Taking out 4 common from $\mathrm{R}_2$=4\left|\begin{array}{ccc}a^2 & b^2 & c^2 \\ a \lambda & b \lambda & c \lambda \\ a^2+\lambda^2-2 a \lambda & b^2+\lambda^2-2 b \lambda & c^2+\lambda^2-2 c \lambda\end{array}\right|$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text { Apply } \mathrm{R}_3 \rightarrow\left[\mathrm{R}_3-\left(\mathrm{R}_1-2 \mathrm{R}_2\right)\right] \\
&=4\left|\begin{array}{lll}
a^2 & b^2 & c^2 \\
a \lambda & b \lambda & c \lambda \\
\lambda^2 & \lambda^2 & \lambda^2
\end{array}\right|
\end{aligned}
$
Taking out $\lambda$ common from $\mathrm{R}_2$ and $\lambda^2$ from $\mathrm{R}_3$.
$
=4 \lambda\left(\lambda^2\right)\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
a^2 & b^2 & c^2 \\
a & b & c \\
1 & 1 & 1
\end{array}\right|
$
$
\begin{aligned}
&=k \lambda\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
a^2 & b^2 & c^2 \\
a & b & c \\
1 & 1 & 1
\end{array}\right| \\
&\Rightarrow k=4 \lambda^2
\end{aligned}
$

$\begin{aligned}$&$\text{ Let }$f($\theta)=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}$1 & \cos $\theta$& 1 \\

&+1$\left(-\sin ^$2 $\theta+$1\right) \\

&=2+\sin 2 $\theta+\cos$2 $\theta

2-$\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=$2-$\sqrt{2} \text{. }$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
If $a, b, c$ are non - zero real numbers and if the system of equations

$\left(a - 1\right)x = y + z$

$\left(b - 1\right)y = x + z$

$\left(c - 1\right)z = x + y$

has a non - trivial solution, then $ab + bc + ca$ equals :
questions.solution:
Given, $\left(a - 1\right)x = y + z ⇒ \left(a - 1\right)x - y - z = 0$

$\left(b - 1\right)y = z + x ⇒ - x + \left(b - 1\right)y - z = 0$

$\left(c - 1\right)z = y + x = - x - y + \left(c - 1\right)z = 0$

For a non-trivial solution

$\left|\begin{cases}a - 1 & - 1 & - 1 \\ - 1 & b - 1 & - 1 \\ - 1 & - 1 & c - 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left|\begin{cases}1 - a & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 - b & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 - c\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left(1 - a\right)\left[\left(1 - b\right)\left(1 - c\right) - 1\right] - 1\left[\left(1 - c\right) - 1\right] + \left[1 - \left(1 - b\right)\right] = 0$

$⇒ 1 - \left(a + b + c\right) + \left(ab + bc + ca\right) - abc - 1 + \left(a + b + c\right) = 0$

$⇒ ab + bc + ca = abc$

questions.q: If $\alpha, \beta \ne 0$, $f\left(n\right) = {\alpha}^{n} + {\beta}^{n}$ and $\left|\begin{cases}3 & 1 + f\left(1\right) & 1 + f\left(2\right) \\ 1 + f\left(1\right) & 1 + f\left(2\right) & 1 + f\left(3\right) \\ 1 + f\left(2\right) & 1 + f\left(3\right) & 1 + f\left(4\right)\end{cases}\right| = K{\left(1 - \alpha\right)}^{2}{\left(1 - \beta\right)}^{2}{\left(\alpha - \beta\right)}^{2}$, then $K$ is equal to

$f\left(1\right) = \alpha + \beta, f\left(2\right) = {\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2}, f\left(3\right) = {\alpha}^{3} + {\beta}^{3}, f\left(4\right) = {\alpha}^{4} + {\beta}^{4}$

So, the given determinant can be written as

If the system of linear equations :

& x_1+2 x_2+3 x_3=6 \\
& x_1+3 x_2+5 x_3=9 \\
& 2 x_1+5 x_2+a x_3=b
\end{aligned}$

is consistent and has infinite number of solutions, then :
options:

$b=15, a$ can be any real number

$a \in R-\{8\}$ and $b \in R-\{15\}$

$a=8, b=15$
questions.solution:
Given system of equations can be written in matrix form as $\mathrm{AX}=\mathrm{B}$ where $\mathrm{A}=\left(\begin{array}{lll}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 2 & 5 & a\end{array}\right)$ and $\mathrm{B}=\left(\begin{array}{l}6 \\ 9 \\ b\end{array}\right)$
Since, system is consistent and has infinitely many solutions
$\therefore(\operatorname{adj} . \mathrm{A}) \mathrm{B}=0$\begin{aligned}$& \Rightarrow$\left(\begin{array}{ccc}$3 a-25 & 15-2 a & 1 \\
10-a & a-6 & -2 \\
-1 & -1 & 1
\end{array}\right)$\left(\begin{array}{l}$6 \\
9 \\
b
\end{array}\right)=$\left(\begin{array}{l}$0 \\
0 \\
0
\end{array}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow-6-9+b=0 \Rightarrow b=15 \\
& $\text{ and }$6(10-a)+9(a-6)-2(b)=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 60-6 a+9 a-54-30=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 3 a=24 \Rightarrow a=8
\end{aligned}

Hence, $a=8, b=15$.

questions.q: If $a, b, c$ are sides of a scalene triangle, then the value of $\left|\begin{array}{lll}a & b & c \\ b & c & a \\ c & a & b\end{array}$\right|$ is :$
questions.solution:
$
\begin{aligned}
&\left|\begin{array}{lll}
a & b & c \\
b & c & a \\
c & a & b
\end{array}\right|=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
a+b+c & a+b+c & a+b+c \\
b & c & a \\
c & a & b
\end{array}\right| \\
&=(a+b+c)\left|\begin{array}{lll}
1 & 1 & 1 \\
b & c & a \\
c & a & b
\end{array}\right| \\
&=(a+b+c)\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
0 & 0 & 1 \\
b-c & c-a & a \\
c-a & a-b & b
\end{array}\right| \\
&=(a+b+c)\left[a b+b c+c a-a^2-b^2-c^2\right] \\
&=-(a+b+c)\left[(a-b)^2+(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2\right]
\end{aligned}
$
Since $a, b, c$ are sides of $a$ scalene triangle, therefore at least two of the $a, b, c$ will be unequal.
$\begin{array}{ll}\therefore \quad & (a-b)^2+(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2>0 \\ & \text { Also } a+b+c>0 \\ \therefore \quad & -(a+b+c)\left[(a-b)^2+\right. \\ & \left.(b-c)^2+(c-a)^2\right] < 0\end{array}$

& x+2 y+3 z=10 \\
& x+2 y+\lambda z=0

has a unique solution, then $\lambda$ is not equal to
questions.solution:
Given system of equations is

$\begin{aligned}$& x+y+z=6 \\
& x+2 y+3 z=10 \\
& x+2 y+\lambda z=0
\end{aligned}

It has unique solution.

$\begin{aligned}$& \therefore $\left|\begin{array}{lll}1 & 1 & 1 \\

\end{aligned}

$x+2 a y+a z=0$x+3 b y+b z=0$x+4 c y+c z=0$
 has a non-zero solution, then $\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}$
options:
satisfy $a+2 b+3 c=0$

are in A.P.

are in G.P.

are in H.P.
questions.solution:
$\left|\begin{array}{lll}1 & 2 \mathrm{a} & \mathrm{a} \\ 1 & 3 \mathrm{~b} & \mathrm{~b} \\ 1 & 4 \mathrm{c} & \mathrm{c}\end{array}\right|=0 \quad \mathrm{C}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_2-2 \mathrm{C}_3\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 0 & \mathrm{a} \\ 1 & \mathrm{~b} & \mathrm{~b} \\ 1 & 2 \mathrm{c} & \mathrm{c}\end{array}\right|=0 \quad \mathrm{R}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{R}_3-\mathrm{R}_2, \mathrm{R}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{R}_2-\mathrm{R}_1\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 0 & a \\ 0 & b & b-a \\ 0 & 2 c-b & c-b\end{array}\right|=0b(c-b)-(b-a)(2 c-b)=0$
On simplification,

$\frac{2}{\mathrm{~b}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{a}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{c}}\therefore \mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}$ are in Harmonic Progression.
